hypothesis:
Measure the 3x MLP arm in one slot by giving up the autotune throughput instead of fighting the wall clock for it.

Two attempts have now died without scoring. t0435 ran 3x cold and was killed before the locked eval; t0438 ran it against the warmed cache, got further -- its error list no longer contains 'expected one nonce-bound locked evaluation, found 0' -- and was killed during evaluation. The reason is that the eval path compiles its own graph, separate from training, and neither run got far enough to cache it. A third attempt might finish the job, but three slots for one measurement is not worth it when reverting the compile mode costs a known -0.00067.

The prize is large. t0438 reached 3057 steps against the champion's 2806, +8.94%. Without autotune that should be roughly 3023 steps, +7.7%, which the token law credits at -0.00436. The 5x arm measured capacity at -0.002872 for a step of ratio, so if capacity is locally linear the 3x capacity debit is about +0.00287 and the net is around -0.0015 -- promotable even after the handicap.
change_summary: MLP_RATIO = 3 with both width sites parameterised (hidden 2048 -> 1536), and torch.compile reverted from the champion's max-autotune to default. The revert is what makes this a one-slot experiment: max-autotune leaves ~76s of wall-clock headroom against the 660s safety timeout and any GEMM-shape change is a cache miss that exceeds it, which is how t0434, t0435, t0436 and t0438 all died after completing their full training. Dry-run against the champion source patched both sites and parsed.
expected_val_bpb_effect:
Predicted raw delta about -0.0015, from -0.00436 throughput plus +0.00287 capacity, where the capacity figure is transferred from the 5x arm under a linearity assumption I cannot check with two points.
I have to weaken the sharpness I claimed earlier. The two 3x runs gave 2973 and 2057... correction: 2973 and 3057 steps for the SAME model, a 2.83% spread, which through the token law is 0.0017 bpb -- larger than the noise floor. I had written that such a discrepancy would mean the throughput term is not as knowable as I was treating it. There are two readings and I cannot separate them here: either step counts on this box carry ~3% run-to-run variance, which would undermine every throughput-corrected residual computed today, or the cold run used partially-autotuned kernels while the warm run used fully cached better ones, which is benign and specific to those two runs. The second is more likely because the runs differed exactly in cache state, but I am not treating it as settled.
Consequence: I expect a win but will not treat a result anywhere in -0.003 to 0.000 as surprising, and the confirmation runs matter more than usual.
risk:
The capacity estimate is transferred from a single measurement on the other side of the incumbent, under an assumption of local linearity that two points cannot test. Capacity is more likely convex -- steeper below 4 than above -- in which case the debit exceeds +0.00287 and this lands nearer zero or loses. That is the honest downside and it is why I pre-registered the convex case as my expectation before t0438 ran.
Second: if this wins, it wins WITHOUT the autotune throughput the current champion carries. Promoting it would trade a +1.14% compile-level gain for a +7.7% architectural one, which is the right trade, but the successor would then want autotune restored on top -- and that combination has never been measured and would face the same wall-clock problem from a new shape. I would rather bank the architectural win first and treat re-adding autotune as a separate, later question than bundle two changes I cannot separate.
